The three-layer metamaterial design achieves absorptivity greater than 90% from 5.66 GHz to 15.10 GHz.
The metamaterial is only loaded on the weak current area of the antenna ground to reduce RCS without deteriorating radiation performance.
The proposed antenna with metamaterials exhibits ultra-broad band RCS reduction from 4.72 GHz to 18 GHz for both x-polarized and y-polarized incidence.
The maximum RCS reduction achieved is 18.4 dB at 8.7 GHz for x-polarized incidence and 22.5 dB at 6.3 GHz for y-polarized incidence.
The 3-dB beamwidths of the antenna with metamaterials are reduced from 156 degrees to 80 degrees in the E-plane and from 62 degrees to 57 degrees in the H-plane at 5.65 GHz.
The gain of the antenna with metamaterials is improved from 6.06 dBi to 8.27 dBi due to the coupling effect between the slot and the metamaterial structure.
Compared to other antennas, the proposed antenna has the broadest RCS reduction bandwidth of 4.7 GHz to 18 GHz (RCSR>5dB) and the highest gain improvement of 2.2 dB.
The metamaterial unit cell is composed of orthogonal double split-ring resonators separated by three lossy dielectric substrates, with a metal ground plane on the bottom layer.
The absorption mechanism of the metamaterial is based on the interference of the reflected and refracted waves from the different layers.
The proposed antenna with metamaterials has potential applications in wireless military communications where low observability and high performance are desired.
Simulated and measured results show good agreement in terms of impedance bandwidth, radiation patterns, and RCS reduction performance.
The fabricated prototypes of the common antenna and the antenna with metamaterials were measured using a vector network analyzer and standard-gain horn antennas.
The measured impedance bandwidth of the antenna with metamaterials is 5.8% (5.49 GHz to 5.82 GHz), slightly wider than the 4.8% (5.54 GHz to 5.81 GHz) of the common antenna.
The measured 3-dB beamwidth of the antenna with metamaterials is reduced from 142 degrees to 56 degrees in the E-plane and from 54 degrees to 48 degrees in the H-plane at 5.65 GHz.
The measured maximum RCS reduction is 18.4 dB at 8.7 GHz for x-polarized incidence and 22.5 dB at 6.3 GHz for y-polarized incidence.
